framing.lineOfInquiry: Sahil Bhatia (P00060) may have been involved in the incident recorded in CASE035
framing.alternate: Sahil Bhatia (P00060) was not involved — the evidence has an innocent explanation
framing.note: KRONOS starts from the presumption of innocence. The line of inquiry and the alternates are tested against the same records; neither is a finding, and the strengths are not probabilities.

alternateHypotheses.title: The money has a legitimate explanation
alternateHypotheses.statement: The flagged money movements of Sahil Bhatia have an ordinary purpose (salary, rent, property, business) or belong to a co-holder of the account.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: Flagged NEFT ₹52,000 on 2025-05-02 15:31 has a stated purpose 'salary' — Stated purpose 'salary' may be a legitimate explanation; verify supporting documents.

alternateHypotheses.test: Obtain full statements, invoices or agreements and KYC; confirm the stated purpose with the counter-party.

alternateHypotheses.title: The contact was routine, not coordination
alternateHypotheses.statement: Sahil Bhatia's calls and messages reflect a long-standing relationship (family, work, business), not planning of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Moderate

evidence.text: In contact with Pankaj Arora since 2025-04-24, 29 days before the incident (13 calls, 12 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Gurpreet Chauhan since 2025-04-29, 24 days before the incident (4 calls, 3 messages) — a long-standing relationship
In contact with Nisha Kapoor since 2025-05-02, 21 days before the incident (8 calls, 2 messages) — a long-standing relationship

alternateHypotheses.test: Examine message content and the timing of contact relative to the incident; establish the relationship.

alternateHypotheses.title: Named or given a role in error
alternateHypotheses.statement: Sahil Bhatia was named in the FIR, or assigned a role, without an independent basis.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded in the FIR as victim, not as accused
Recorded in the FIR as witness, not as accused

alternateHypotheses.test: Re-examine the FIR and statements; record the person's statement and the informant's basis for naming them.

alternateHypotheses.title: Was near the scene for a routine reason
alternateHypotheses.statement: Sahil Bhatia was near the scene because they regularly go there (home, work, market), not because of the incident.
alternateHypotheses.label: Weak

evidence.text: Recorded within 1 km of the scene on 31 other days (24 Apr – 21 Jun), so presence there is part of their routine

alternateHypotheses.test: Establish why the person is regularly there (address, employment, shop) and compare the incident-time visit with their usual pattern (time of day, duration).

alternatesConsideredNotSupported.title: Someone else used the phone or handset

comparison.verdict: Every supporting item could be explained by at least one alternate, although the line of inquiry is stronger on weight (0.73 vs 0.44). Test the alternates before relying on it.

confidence.note: Evidential balance compares weighted supporting vs contradicting evidence; it is not a probability of guilt. Prior records are excluded from this score.

note: Each hypothesis is tested from both sides to reduce confirmation bias. Confidence scores are evidential balance (not probability of guilt). Human review is required.
